title: Normalized ordinary restriction of strict quotient and Roos chain models
statement: Fix ell and E as above [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let s:S -> V be weakly etale and i:V -> T an immersion of qcqs schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism], and put r=i s. Use the actual ordinary ringed pullback F_r, complex pullback and left derived pullback of [def-fix-qcqs-completion-ordinary-models], with independent scheme and coefficient universes. Then F_r preserves finite limits and colimits, and its specified completed coefficient map is invertible. There exist a natural strict quotient-tower isomorphism tau:F_r(tower_T P) ~= tower_S(F_r P), a natural Roos chain isomorphism chi:F_r(roos_T P) ~= roos_S(F_r P). Tau preserves the specified strict quotient augmentations. On both the product and shifted-product coordinates chi is exactly the canonical product comparison followed by the product of the components of tau. The towers and Roos functors are those of [def-pur-integral-derived-operations].

source.place: Tag 09AA, lemma-closed-immersion, clause (1); Tag 09BL, lemma-closed-immersion-affines-apply; weakly etale slice restriction in Tag 09AE, definition-extension-zero; Bhatt–Scholze Lemma 6.5.8(1). Tensor comparison: sites-cohomology.tex Tags 06YY, lemma-derived-base-change, and 07A4, lemma-pullback-tensor-product.

proof.text: Apply qcqsOrdinaryRestrictionExact for preservation of all small limits and the fixed coefficient-map isomorphism. Finite limits follow by specialization. Finite colimits are preserved because ordinaryPull is the left adjoint in ordinaryAdjunction; no geometric input is needed for this colimit clause.
Obtain the natural strict quotient-tower isomorphism tau and its augmentation equation from qcqsOrdinaryQuotientRestriction.

Use the existing scalarRoosMap and podReindexingRoosCoordinates on each quotient tower. Its degreewise matrix is the additive biproduct comparison followed by the two countable-product comparisons, so it is invertible when ordinaryPull preserves countable products. Compose with integralOperationsRoosFunctor.mapIso(tau). Naturality is podReindexingRoosNaturality followed by the naturality of tau. The mapping-cocone first and shifted-second coordinate equations for integralOperationsRoosMap, followed by podReindexingRoosCoordinates, give precisely the two required product comparison equations. This argument needs neither derived descent nor exact countable products. For the exact shifted index j + -1, product extensionality applied to scalarRoosMap_existsUnique gives the coordinate formula directly at arbitrary compatible degrees; no dependent index rewrite or sign change is used.

proof_origin.place: Tag 08TC; scalarRoosMap and podReindexingRoosCoordinates, with the degreewise additive biproduct/product matrix argument and the original geometric and quotient steps isolated separately.

lean.statement:
theorem qcqsOrdinaryRestrictionModels
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (E : Type u) [Field E]
    [Algebra ℚ_[l] E] [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] E]
    {S V T : Scheme.{t}} [CompactSpace S] [QuasiSeparatedSpace S]
    [CompactSpace V] [QuasiSeparatedSpace V] [CompactSpace T] [QuasiSeparatedSpace T]
    (s : S ⟶ V) (i : V ⟶ T) [WeaklyEtale s] [IsImmersion i] :
    let r := s ≫ i
    PreservesFiniteLimits (ordinaryPull l E r) ∧
    PreservesFiniteColimits (ordinaryPull l E r) ∧
    IsIso (ordinaryCoefficientMap l E r) ∧
    (∃ (τ : tower l E T none ⋙
          (Functor.whiskeringRight ℕᵒᵖ (Cx l E T none) (Cx l E S none)).obj
            (ordinaryComplexPull l E r) ≅
          ordinaryComplexPull l E r ⋙ tower l E S none)
        (χ : roos l E T none ⋙ ordinaryComplexPull l E r ≅
          ordinaryComplexPull l E r ⋙ roos l E S none),
        (∀ (P : Cx l E T none) (n : ℕ),
          (ordinaryComplexPull l E r).map (((augmentation l E T none).app P).app (op n)) ≫
              (τ.hom.app P).app (op n) =
            ((augmentation l E S none).app ((ordinaryComplexPull l E r).obj P)).app (op n)) ∧
        (∀ P : Cx l E T none,
          χ.hom.app P ≫ CochainComplex.mappingCocone.fst
              (ordinaryRoosEndomorphism l E ((ordinaryComplexPull l E r).obj P)) =
            (ordinaryComplexPull l E r).map
                (CochainComplex.mappingCocone.fst (ordinaryRoosEndomorphism l E P)) ≫
              piComparison (ordinaryComplexPull l E r)
                (fun n : ℕ ↦ ((tower l E T none).obj P).obj (op n)) ≫
              Limits.Pi.map (fun n : ℕ ↦ (τ.hom.app P).app (op n))) ∧
        (∀ (P : Cx l E T none) (i : ℤ),
          (χ.hom.app P).f i ≫
              (CochainComplex.mappingCocone.snd
                (ordinaryRoosEndomorphism l E ((ordinaryComplexPull l E r).obj P))).v
                  i (i + -1) rfl =
            (ordinaryPull l E r).map
                ((CochainComplex.mappingCocone.snd (ordinaryRoosEndomorphism l E P)).v
                  i (i + -1) rfl) ≫
              (piComparison (ordinaryComplexPull l E r)
                (fun n : ℕ ↦ ((tower l E T none).obj P).obj (op n))).f (i + -1) ≫
              (Limits.Pi.map (fun n : ℕ ↦ (τ.hom.app P).app (op n))).f (i + -1)))
